@AThousandShips To be clear, you can review/approve other people's PRs like any other user (not blocked by [godotengine](https://github.com/godotengine))(see: [Approving a pull request with required reviews](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/approving-a-pull-request-with-required-reviews)). The difference is: an approval by non-member (of [godotengine](https://github.com/godotengine)) doesn't allow merging the PR, as at least one member-approval is required (with exception for the owners I think (you know, the super-members:smile:), they could merge anything as they like (I mean technically they have such power)). But a non-member's review (approval is a form of review) is still a valuable feedback (especially when they gave some suggestions; like after seeing an approval following some changes I'd assume their previous suggestions/comments were addressed).

issue_context.title: ImageTexture class reference has a pointless section
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.2

### System information

Ubuntu 22.04.1 LTS

### Issue description

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/85438892/47baf956-c28c-4f8f-aed5-c515528d4ed6)

Normally, the "Property descriptions" section would be skipped in this case, but because there's an overridden property (which doesn't need a description) this section shows up without needing to.

### Steps to reproduce

Open ImageTexture's class reference.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments:
This should be the relevant section:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/fd4a06c51555904104b18494d0224f450d74fe2a/editor/editor_help.cpp#L918-L930

The property doc indicates if it is overriding and should be possible to check any are non-overriding

review_comments: You should break here, no reason to continue iteration

I'd suggest combining this into `prop.overridden || ...` and then just removing the second if (i.e. just leaving the contents of that block below), don't think scripts can override properties anyway (the override here just deals with the default value as far as I know)

I almost want to move `prop.name.begins_with("_") && prop.description.strip_edges().is_empty()` to some method on the `PropertyDoc` class to make this more readable. Like

`cd.is_script_doct && prop.is_undocumented_private` or something like that
Is it used anywhere else? If not it's not really worth it I'd say
doesn't look like it. I updated the code!
The grouping is not needed, && has higher precedence
